facts.statement: Mesetasaurus is known from two well-preserved tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, the type species Mesetasaurus protector, known from two well-preserved caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered in the 1980s.
The species was formally described in 2026.
facts.quote: They were described as belonging to a new genus and species of titanosaurian dinosaur in 2026.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of two tail vertebrae, likely the third and sixth in the series.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Mesetasaurus protector consiste de dos vértebras caudales, que probablemente corresponden a la tercera y sexta posición

facts.statement: The generic name Mesetasaurus refers to the fossil locality, Meseta de Artigas.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico, Mesetasaurus, hace referencia a la localidad donde se encontraron los fósiles, Meseta de Artigas.

facts.statement: The specific name protector honors the Uruguayan hero José Gervasio Artigas.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, protector, hace referencia al prócer uruguayo José Artigas, también conocido por su título de "Protector de los Pueblos Libres"

facts.statement: Mesetasaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous (potentially Coniacian to Maastrichtian) in Uruguay.
facts.quote: Mesetasaurus () is a genus of aeolosaurin titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs known from the Guichón Formation (Late Cretaceous, potentially Coniacian to Maastrichtian) of Paysandú Department, Uruguay.

facts.statement: The presence of Mesetasaurus supports a Coniacian to Maastrichtian age for the Guichón Formation.
Mesetasaurus is classified as an aeolosaurin titanosaurian sauropod.
facts.quote: Mesetasaurus () is a genus of aeolosaurin titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs

facts.statement: Mesetasaurus belongs to the clade Aeolosaurini.
Phylogenetic analysis places Mesetasaurus deeply nested within the clade Aeolosaurini.
Some researchers have historically debated a Lower Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation based on similarities with the Migues Formation.
facts.quote: Some authors have historically suggested a Lower Cretaceous (Aptian–Albian) age due to similarities with the Migues Formation.

facts.statement: The discovery of dinosaur eggshells similar to Sphaerovum led researchers to favor a Late Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation.
facts.quote: The discovery of dinosaur eggshells in the formation similar to Sphaerovum prompted later researchers to favor a Late Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation.
